sources.entry: Site Reliability Engineering: How Google Runs Production Systems

summary.name: Site Reliability Engineering (Google SRE Book)
summary.one_liner: A book by Google's Site Reliability Engineering team on the principles and practices used to run large production systems reliably, scalably, and efficiently.
use_cases: learning how Google runs production systems
guiding reliability work in an engineering organization
understanding the impact of AI on reliability
summary.what_it_does: The page describes a completely rewritten edition of Site Reliability Engineering, edited by Betsy Beyer, Chris Jones, Christof Leng, David Huska, Jennifer Petoff and Niall Richard Murphy. It is written by key members of Google's SRE team and explains the company's current SRE practices and how they have evolved over the decade since the first publication. The new edition covers the value of reliability, cloud reliability, and the impact of AI. It presents the principles and practices Google engineers use to keep some of the world's largest systems scalable, reliable, and efficient, and says these lessons apply to other organizations.
notable: Rewritten edition by Google's SRE team, covering a decade of evolution
New coverage of cloud reliability and the impact of AI
Explains how Google runs some of the world's largest production systems
